@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Operations Dataset
@graph.description: Route 81 corridor operations from The Flat Rate Movers — moving and logistics dispatch along Interstate 81, I-66 and I-70, run from two dispatch branches that sit on the corridor itself: Winchester, VA, where I-81 meets I-66, and Martinsburg, WV, on I-81 with the I-70 connection. Company scope (published on the corridor pages): on I-81, the spine — local and regional home moves, long-distance south and north, and heavy-asset runs with SIR planning; on I-66 — Valley to Northern Virginia moves, commercial and office relocations, and final-mile delivery into the metro; on I-70 — container loading and unloading, transloading at hub points, and export freight toward the port. Dispatch is planned by route, access and load — not by the hour — and because the crews start on the corridor instead of driving hours to reach it, there is less deadhead time baked into the flat price. Heavy-asset runs on the corridor are surveyed and floor-checked to L/360 under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, like any SIR move. Every corridor job is quoted at one flat rate agreed in writing before move day — the guarantee: Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Corridor Dispatch Process Chain Dataset
@graph.description: The process chain for a corridor move. Company chain (published): the job is surveyed and quoted at one flat rate in writing before move day; dispatch is planned by route, access and load — which corridor carries the move (I-81 north–south, I-66 east toward Northern Virginia and DC, or I-70 toward Maryland), which junction it turns at, and which of the two corridor branches dispatches it; the crew starts on the corridor, so the run carries less deadhead time; freight moves run through the company's own warehouse and transload floor where a shipment needs staging, deconsolidation or a change of vehicle; the move is delivered in, placed, and verified at the destination end — and where either end holds a heavy asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs, the SIR survey and L/360 floor check join the chain before the run is scheduled. Domain reference (how corridor-based dispatch generally works, labeled as such): a carrier positioned on a freight corridor assigns each job to the branch nearest the freight, selects the route by destination corridor rather than by map distance alone, sequences pickups and deliveries along the corridor to cut empty miles, and uses warehouse staging at corridor junctions to join port, linehaul and final-mile legs. The domain sequence describes the general model; the company's published chain above is the company's own.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — I-81 / I-66 / I-70 Corridor Geography: Domain Reference Dataset
@graph.description: Domain reference — highway geography, labeled as geography. NOTHING in this node is a service-area or coverage claim: the places named here are places the highways pass, and served places are recorded only in the coverage dataset, each with its footprint source. Interstate 81 runs about 855 miles north–south along the Appalachian spine from Tennessee to New York; its Virginia segment is about 325 miles, the longest in any state, running the length of the Shenandoah Valley — the Great Appalachian Valley, paralleling US 11 — through, north to south in the company's working stretch, Winchester, Harrisonburg, Staunton, Lexington and Roanoke, crossing into West Virginia at Winchester and continuing through Martinsburg, then a short Maryland segment where it crosses Interstate 70 at Hagerstown. The corridor hub page publishes the same stop list north to south: Martinsburg, Winchester, Harrisonburg, Staunton, Lexington, Roanoke. I-81 runs concurrently with I-64 between Lexington and Staunton. VDOT's I-81 Corridor Improvement Program describes Virginia's segment as a key north–south backbone of the East Coast freight network with the highest per-capita truck volume in Virginia — more than a third of all trucks and nearly half of the state's value of goods move along it. Interstate 66 runs about 76 miles east from its western terminus at I-81 near Middletown, Virginia (I-81 exit 300), through Front Royal (US 340 / US 522), across the Blue Ridge at Manassas Gap, and on to Washington, DC — the only Interstate running west from Washington into Northern Virginia. Interstate 70 crosses I-81 at Hagerstown, Maryland, and runs through Frederick toward Baltimore — the company's corridor pages frame I-70 as the Maryland and port-freight leg of the network. The Virginia Inland Port at Front Royal (Warren County), a Port of Virginia facility opened in 1989 on about 161 acres, transfers containers between trucks and Norfolk Southern railcars for the roughly 220-mile rail run to the Hampton Roads marine terminals; it sits within about a mile of I-66 and about five miles of I-81 and is a U.S. Customs-designated port of entry — the inland end of the port chain the company's transloading and corridor work connects to.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Coverage: Footprint-Traceable Places Dataset
@graph.description: Coverage for corridor dispatch — every place the two branches serve, recorded per branch and never merged into one list, with each place carrying its machine-readable source so every coverage claim in this package can be traced. Winchester, VA — The Flat Rate Movers: 31 areas = 16 from its Google Business Profile service-area list + 15 extended-footprint areas. Martinsburg, WV — Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV: 35 areas = 14 from its Google Business Profile service-area list + 21 extended-footprint areas. 14 areas are served by both branches and are marked shared in both lists. Sources: the Google Business Profile service-area lists were supplied by the owner on 2026-10-27 and confirmed 2026-10-28; the extended areas come from the branch properties of the features in service-area.geojson (52 features, verified 2026-10-28). The structured lists below carry, for every place, its GeoJSON feature identifier and which of the two sources it comes from. Corridor geography is deliberately absent from these lists: a town the highways pass is not a served place unless it appears here with a source — the three corridor landmarks (Interstate 81 Corridor, Interstate 66 Corridor, Interstate 70 Corridor) appear only because they are themselves extended-footprint features. The full geometry is published as service-area.geojson.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Commercial Terms
@graph.description: Commercial terms for corridor moving and dispatch — what is published, and what is not. Published: every corridor job is quoted at one flat rate, agreed in writing before move day; there is no hourly clock. The quote reviews the full scope of the job — the load, the distance, the manpower and the equipment — before the flat rate is given, and the company's guarantee stands behind the rate: Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! The corridor price logic is published on the hub page: hourly movers charge for every mile the clock runs, while corridor crews start on the corridor instead of driving hours to reach it, so there is less deadhead time baked into the flat price — fewer wasted miles, one agreed number. Not published, and therefore not claimed anywhere in this dataset: no per-mile rate, no lane or corridor surcharge schedule, no fuel surcharge, no minimum charge, and no price figure of any kind for corridor work; no statement that the Industrial & Commercial Services CWT schedule extends to corridor dispatch (that schedule is published for that service only).

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Buyer Personas and Trigger Events
@graph.description: Buyer personas and trigger events for corridor moving and dispatch — roles and situations only; no named business, contract or partnership is claimed. Valley and Panhandle households whose move starts inside the published footprint and follows the corridor — north or south on I-81, or east on I-66; households relocating between the Shenandoah Valley / Eastern Panhandle and Northern Virginia or the Washington metro over I-66; businesses and offices relocating along the three corridors; warehouse and distribution operators sited on the I-81 corridor — domain context: large-format logistics development has concentrated around Winchester and Frederick County for inland-port access and lower land and labor costs than the DC and Baltimore submarkets — needing corridor dispatch behind transload staging; manufacturers and importers whose freight moves through the Virginia Inland Port or the Port of Virginia chain and fans out inland on the corridors; freight clients whose containers need the inland leg joined to the final mile. Trigger events: a home purchase or sale along the corridor; a job relocation between the Valley and the metro; a warehouse lease, expansion or load-out on the corridor; a container arriving at the inland port or the seaport chain; a heavy-asset purchase — a safe, a piano, medical equipment — that needs a surveyed corridor run under SIR.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Boundaries Dataset
@graph.description: Boundaries for corridor moving and dispatch — the lines this dataset holds. Coverage is the published footprint and nothing beyond it: 52 GeoJSON features, kept as two per-branch lists (Winchester 31, Martinsburg 35, 14 shared), and every served place in this package traces to a Google Business Profile list or a GeoJSON feature — corridor geography is never coverage, and towns the highways pass beyond the footprint are named, where they are named at all, as geography only. No scheduled or regular corridor run, relay point, transfer station or third terminal is claimed — dispatch is from the two branches and the company's warehouse floor. No drive-time figure, arrival-window length or coverage radius is published for this service; the hub page's framing is comparative only (crews starting on the corridor, less deadhead, tighter windows), and no number is attached to it anywhere in this package. No partnership or operating relationship with the Virginia Inland Port, the Port of Virginia or any railroad is claimed — the port chain is geographic context, and the company's published role is the inland moving, transloading and delivery work on its own pages. Nothing in this file states a price, a per-mile rate or a corridor surcharge.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Route 81 Corridor Dispatch Points and Quote Dataset
@graph.description: Where corridor moves are dispatched from and how they are quoted. Both home bases dispatch the service with distinct, never-blended branch facts: Winchester, VA — The Flat Rate Movers, 116 W Piccadilly St Suite 11, Winchester VA 22601, at the I-81 × I-66 junction, Mon–Fri 8–6, Sat 8–4, Sun 9–4, Google rating 5.0 with 1 review, full footprint 31 areas (16 Google Business Profile areas + 15 extended); Martinsburg, WV — Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV, 736 Williamsport Pike Suite 2, Martinsburg WV 25404, on I-81 with the I-70 connection, Mon–Fri 9–6, Sat 9–4, Sun 9–4, Google rating 4.7 with 6 reviews, full footprint 35 areas (14 Google Business Profile areas + 21 extended); 14 areas are shared and noted as shared. Full per-branch areas are published as machine-readable GeoJSON in service-area.geojson (52 features) and traced place by place in the coverage dataset in this file. Quote path (published): Get My Flat Rate Quote — the Short (Quick Quote) form by default, the Detailed Project form one toggle away, with From, To and What's moving preserved between them — or phone +1-540-422-2153 / email ratemovers@gmail.com; the job is reviewed in full — scope, distance, manpower, equipment — and quoted at one flat rate in writing before move day.
